What to look for (DXC issue 3706)

`j` is declared and never written, then used as the element index of a
StructuredBuffer. DXC accepts this with no diagnostic at all and exits 0.

In the DXC panes, find the RawBufferLoad call in @main. Its operands are
    (opcode, handle, index, elementOffset, mask, alignment)
and the INDEX operand -- the one straight after the handle -- is the
compiler's placeholder-for-undefined value. That is the whole report.

Read the INDEX slot specifically, not just "is there a placeholder somewhere
in the line". One in the *elementOffset* slot is required, not a defect: for a
ByteAddressBuffer the DXIL validator rejects anything else there
(Instr.CoordinateCountForRawTypedBuf). Checking the wrong slot makes correct
shaders look broken -- that mistake was made once already, on DXC issue 3009.

Also worth noting:

  * On a local build the module passes DXIL validation and is signed. The
    validator does police this placeholder value, but only as a value STORED
    to a UAV (Instr.UndefinedValueForUAVStore), never as a load index.
    Compiler Explorer cannot show that half: its DXC panes report
    "DXIL.dll not found", so validation is skipped there.

  * DXC already has the front-end check. Add -Wall or -Wuninitialized to
    either DXC pane and it reports the read of `j` and points at the
    declaration. It is simply not in the default warning set.

  * FXC pane: the predecessor compiler rejects this source outright.

  * Clang pane runs -fsyntax-only, because its DXIL backend cannot lower a
    vertex stage and the errors it produces are about that, not about this
    issue. It still diagnoses the return statement itself (sign conversion),
    so the front end is reaching that expression -- it just has nothing to
    say about `j` being read before it is written.
